text:
Maria: quick heads-up — during the compact-layer rollout a small percentage of prod nodes started refusing the image, error shows `signature verification failed: nonce mismatch` :/
Ashok: ugh. do we have the cosign key id that signed that digest?
Sam: I saw the alerts, attaching what I grabbed from the registry: `sha256:8f3a...` verified by key `projects/redwood/signer/keys/keystore-v2`
Kevin: @Maria can you confirm whether the rollback will re-use the same signed layers or produce new layer digests? if new digests we need to re-sign before pushing or consumers will fail.
Maria: plan was to create a slimline nonces-layer (same content but rebuilt) to avoid the vuln in glibc. that changes layer digest. I didn't realize downstream sig policy enforces nonce equality.
Luis: we have two problems: (1) RBAC on the keystore limits who can sign; (2) our audit logs show the signing op used a wrapped key with a transient nonce — the verifier expects a deterministic nonce.
Sam: CosignBot reported `signature: invalid - nonce field present but mismatch`. CosignBot: signature verification failed for `sha256:8f3a...` - expected nonce 0x9a3b, got 0x4f2c.
Ashok: Any chance this is a recent KMS operator change? We rotated the keystore provider last week (KMS: aws-kms -> customer-managed HSM) and added key-wrapping.
Kevin: That would explain it — some KMS wrappers produce ephemeral nonces. We must ensure signing policy strips or normalizes nonce, or update verifier to tolerate new metadata.
Maria: short-term mitigation: revert consumers to the last fully signed image (pre-compact). Are we comfortable with that rollback window?
Luis: Oncall-Bot: rolling back to image tag `release-2026-03-17` will take ~5m per region with our current deploy pipeline. Need approval from security and runtime leads before doing across all regions.
Sam: Security note: if we re-sign layers using the new HSM we must record the signing event in the audit log with the KV references and cosign attestation. Otherwise compliance will flag it.
Ashok: Proposal: 1) revert consumers to `release-2026-03-17` now (canary in us-west-2) 2) run a small re-sign flow for the rebuilt slim layer but keep it in a staging repo until verifier changes land 3) add a verifier compatibility flag to allow the wrapped-nonce signatures for 72h while we rotate.
Kevin: +1 to the staged re-sign and verifier opt-in. We should also create a short-lived RBAC grant for `signer-service` to call KMS:Decrypt/wrapKey only for the re-sign job and audit the calls.
Maria: ok i'll kick off canary rollback in us-west-2 in 5m. @Ashok can you open a temporary RBAC request for `signer-service` and include start/end times?
Ashok: opening request now. will scope to `projects/redwood/signing/*` and add a 24h expiry. link: https://internal.redwood/iam/requests/REQ-6123
Sam: dev note: verifier change is small — in `pkg/verifier/nonce.go` add a fallback to ignore nonce field if signature metadata contains `kms-wrapper=true`. will draft PR after rollback.
Luis: i'll capture the audit trail: KMS logs, cosign attestations, deploy events. tagging this incident for the compliance ticket `COMP-1847`.
Kevin: after we're stable let's run a one-day drill to ensure future layer rebuilds don't break signature policies — include build system, cosign, KMS, verifier, and RBAC steps.
Maria: thanks team. i'll post a short incident timeline in #incidents once rollback completes. :thumbsup:
CosignBot: Manual signature check queued for `sha256:8f3a...` - will report back.
Oncall-Bot: Canary rollback started in us-west-2 (deploy id: dpl-9922). ETA 6m.
